Yes, that boundary feels right to me. If I paste the same article back with just a jump-to-a-section bit on the end, or one of those newsletter tracking tails that gets stuck on when I click through from an email, that's still the same article as far as I'm concerned — I'd want it to take me to the one I already saved rather than quietly pile up a near-identical second copy. Those little tails are exactly the kind of noise I'd never want cluttering my collection.

But I wouldn't want it getting too clever and lumping together addresses that really are different pages. If the ending actually changes what I'd see — a different search, a different page of results, a genuinely different view — then that's its own thing and deserves its own bookmark. Losing one of those because the app decided it was "close enough" would be worse than an occasional duplicate.

So: ignore the meaningless tracking-and-jump bits and treat those as the same, but keep genuinely different pages separate. That's the line I'd draw too.
